constitucion.title: Constitución de la República de Honduras, 1982, con las reformas desde 1982 hasta 2004 (Decreto 131 de 11 de enero de 1982)
constitucion.publisher: Tribunal Superior de Cuentas (TSC), Biblioteca Virtual
constitucion.note: Consolidated text with footnotes giving each reforming decree. Art. 202 fixes 128 deputies (Decreto 28-88); art. 236 elects the presidential formula by simple majority; art. 237 sets a four-year term from 27 January; art. 311 has the Congress elect the Supreme Court. Footnote 1 records Decreto 242-2003 adding the referéndum and plebiscito to art. 5, pending ratification in this text.

ley2021.title: Ley Electoral de Honduras, Decreto 35-2021 (La Gaceta No. 35,610, 26 de mayo de 2021)
ley2021.publisher: Tribunal Superior de Cuentas (TSC), Biblioteca Virtual
ley2021.note: Art. 42: a departmental electoral council in each of the 18 departments; art. 44: a municipal electoral council in each of the 298 municipalities; art. 80: voters abroad vote only for President and Designados; art. 193: primaries on the second Sunday of March of the election year; art. 211: general elections on the last Sunday of November; art. 212: the offices elected; arts. 285-288: how the presidential formula, the 128 deputies, the 20 PARLACEN deputies, and the municipal corporations are declared; art. 289: a separate ballot and box for each level.

ley2004.title: Ley Electoral y de las Organizaciones Políticas, Decreto 44-2004 (15 de mayo de 2004)
ley2004.publisher: Tribunal Superior de Cuentas (TSC), Biblioteca Virtual
ley2004.note: Art. 113: party primaries on the third Sunday of February of the election year, run by the Tribunal Supremo Electoral; art. 159: general elections on the last Sunday of November. Replaced by Decreto 35-2021.

municipalidades.title: Ley de Municipalidades, Decreto 134-90, con sus reformas
municipalidades.publisher: Tribunal Superior de Cuentas (TSC), Biblioteca Virtual
municipalidades.note: Art. 25(10): the corporation may call a binding plebiscito of the municipality's citizens; art. 26: a corporation of an alcalde and 4, 6, 8, or 10 regidores by population; art. 59: alcaldes auxiliares of barrios, colonias, aldeas, and caseríos, chosen by the corporation from a terna that a public assembly selects, and patronatos of residents. Its preamble replaces the Ley de Municipalidades y del Régimen Político of 1 April 1927.

lopl.title: Ley Orgánica del Poder Legislativo, Decreto 363-2013 (2014)
lopl.publisher: Tribunal Superior de Cuentas (TSC), Biblioteca Virtual
lopl.note: The Congress of 128 deputies and their substitutes, elected for four years by direct vote; it also elects the officials the Constitution assigns to it.

parlacen.title: Periodos Parlamentarios
parlacen.note: The Parliament's own history of its terms. It says Honduras was the first country to elect deputies to it, in the elections of November 1989, per Punto de Acta No. 850 of the Tribunal Nacional de Elecciones, and lists 20 Honduran deputies by party for each term.

cne.title: Consejo Nacional Electoral: resultados electorales
cne.note: The election authority since 2019 (Tribunal Nacional de Elecciones to 2004, Tribunal Supremo Electoral 2004-2019). Its site and its results portals answer automated clients with a Cloudflare challenge.

classes.name: Presidente y Designados a la Presidencia de la República
classes.name_en: President of the Republic, with the Designados (a single Vice President under the 2002 reform) on the same formula
classes.note: Elected with three Designados (a Vice President under the 2002 reform) on one formula by simple majority, with no runoff (Constitution art. 236; Ley Electoral 2021 art. 285), for four years from 27 January. Hondurans abroad vote only for this office (Ley Electoral 2021 art. 80). first_held is the first election under the 1982 Constitution; earlier presidents back to 1839 are in a span row.

cadence.runoff_rule: Simple majority of valid votes; no runoff (Constitution art. 236; Ley Electoral 2021 art. 285).

classes.name: Diputados al Congreso Nacional
classes.note: 128 deputies and substitutes since 1989 (Constitution art. 202, Decreto 28-88), elected in the 18 departments by open-list proportional representation: a departmental quotient, then largest remainders, with candidates ranked by their individual marks; departments with one seat elect it by simple majority (Ley Electoral 2021 art. 286). Separate ballots for each level since 1993 (art. 289 in the 2021 law).

classes.name: Corporaciones Municipales (regidores)
classes.name_en: Municipal corporations: regidores elected with the alcalde on one list
classes.note: Each party presents one planilla of alcalde, vicealcalde, and 4 to 10 regidores (Ley de Municipalidades art. 26). The list with most votes takes the alcalde and vicealcalde; the regidores are shared by a municipal quotient and largest remainders after deducting the quotient that elected the alcalde (Ley Electoral 2021 art. 288). Separate municipal ballot since 1993; before it, one vote for all levels.

classes.name: Elecciones primarias e internas
classes.name_en: State-run party primaries for president, deputies, and municipal corporations
classes.note: Every party with more than one internal movement must nominate its presidential formula, deputies, and municipal planillas in primaries run by the election authority on the same day (Ley Electoral 2021 arts. 193-195 and 289); parties with one movement nominate without a vote. Internal elections preceded the 2004 law's primaries; first_held is the first primary under that law. The 2008 and 2012 primaries were held in November of the year before the general election under reforms of the 2004 law.

classes.name: Plebiscito y referéndum nacional
classes.note: Instituted by the reform of Constitution art. 5 (Decreto 242-2003); the CNE administers plebiscites and referendums along with primaries and general elections (Ley Electoral 2021 art. 6). None has been held.

classes.name: Plebiscito municipal
classes.disposition_reason: Called and counted by each municipal corporation (Ley de Municipalidades art. 25(10)); no national body compiles or publishes the results.

classes.name: Asamblea Nacional Constituyente
classes.disposition_reason: No official publication of constituent assembly results is online: the election authority's portals start with later general elections, and the 1980 declaratoria of the Tribunal Nacional de Elecciones would have to be found in La Gaceta.
classes.note: The last, elected on 20 April 1980 by department, wrote the 1982 Constitution (Decreto 131 of 11 January 1982) and named the provisional president. Earlier assemblies (among them 1957 and 1965) are in a span row.

dates.note: Constituent assemblies before 1980. Not yet listed.

classes.name: Magistrados de la Corte Suprema de Justicia
classes.disposition_reason: Elected by two thirds of the Congress from a nominating board's list (Constitution arts. 311-312), not by voters.

classes.name: Elecciones de segundo grado del Congreso Nacional
classes.name_en: Officials the Congress elects: the electoral councils, the Attorney General, the auditors, and others
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by the Congress (for the electoral authority, Constitution art. 52), not by voters.

classes.name: Alcaldes auxiliares
classes.name_en: Auxiliary mayors of villages, hamlets, and neighborhoods
classes.disposition_reason: A public assembly proposes a terna and the municipal corporation appoints one of them (Ley de Municipalidades art. 59); there is no ballot or count.

classes.name: Patronatos
classes.name_en: Residents' boards (patronatos) of barrios, colonias, and aldeas
classes.disposition_reason: Civil associations whose boards residents elect in assemblies under municipal and Interior ministry rules (Ley de Municipalidades art. 59); not public elections and no compiled results.
